Kussmaul breathing—rapid, deep, and labored

metabolic acidosis—condition resulting from
either loss of bicarbonate or retention of non-
volatile acid
metabolic alkalosis—condition resulting from
either retention of bicarbonate or loss of non-
volatile acid
pK—the constant degree of dissociation (the
ability of an acid to release its hydrogen ions) for
a given solution; this is a constant amount for
any given solution
respiratory acidosis—condition resulting from
excess acid in the blood secondary to carbon
dioxide retention
respiratory alkalosis—condition resulting from
excess base in the blood secondary to increased
carbon dioxide expiration
